sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18.sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18/no_: Following consultation, the Council found common ground on ending Sudan hostilities to protect civilians, per CN-A. However, the Russian Federation opposed external accountability mechanisms, insisting justice remain with the Sudanese Government, per RU-A. Draft S/2024/826, sponsored by Sierra Leone and the UK, received 14 votes in favour, one against, and no abstentions. China supported the draft, while Russia cast the sole negative vote, preventing adoption. The Russian Federation cited risks of outside interference, whereas China emphasized immediate ceasefire necessity. No further steps were proposed due to the lack of adoption.
sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18.sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18/rus: On 18 November 2024, the Security Council considered draft S/2024/826 to end hostilities in Sudan. Common ground included an immediate ceasefire to protect civilians (CN-A). However, the Russian Federation opposed external accountability mechanisms, insisting justice remain with Sudan's government (RU-A). China supported the draft, noting some concerns were not fully reflected (CN-A). The draft was not adopted due to Russia's sole negative vote. China abstained on other measures, citing insufficient reflection of constructive proposals. The Council will reconvene to address the Personal Envoy's engagement timeline (RU-B).
sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18.sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18/chi: On 18 November 2024, the Security Council consulted on draft S/2024/826 to end Sudan hostilities. Common ground included immediate ceasefire and civilian protection (CN-A). However, the Russian Federation opposed external accountability mechanisms, insisting justice remain with the Sudanese Government (RU-A). China supported the draft but noted some concerns were unaddressed (CN-A). The draft was not adopted due to Russia's veto. Proposed measures included ending hostilities and facilitating humanitarian access. China's caveat was ensuring sovereignty and consultation with Sudan's Government (CN-B). The next step involves resuming consultations with the African Union.
sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18.sudan-civilian-protection-2024-11-18/bot: On 18 November 2024, the Security Council considered draft S/2024/826 to end hostilities in Sudan. Common ground included an immediate ceasefire to protect civilians (CN-A). However, the Russian Federation opposed external accountability mechanisms, insisting justice remain with Sudan's Government (RU-A). China supported the draft but noted some constructive proposals were not fully reflected (CN-B). The draft was not adopted due to Russia's sole negative vote. The vote recorded 14 in favour, one against, and no abstentions. Proposed measures included facilitating humanitarian access. China's caveat was to ensure Council action rests on consultation with Sudan's Government (CN-B). Russia's caveat required agreement with central authorities and time for Personal Envoy Ramtane Lamamra to engage relevant actors (RU-B).
